overview:
CA-16 covers much of Silicon Valley, including San Jose, and leans heavily Democratic with a partisan lean of about 25 points. Incumbent Sam Liccardo is running for re-election against Republican Peter Soulé, who has raised only a few hundred dollars. Liccardo has raised roughly $3.5 million and holds more than $2 million on hand, giving him an overwhelming resource advantage.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, fundraising, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win near 97 percent. The expected margin is roughly 27 points Democratic, placing the race firmly in the Safe Democratic column. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, though the structural advantages here make an upset highly unlikely.
